turns.response_html:
That is an ultrasonic mist maker (also known as an ultrasonic fogger). While they are often sold for fish tanks or indoor fountains, they serve a specific aesthetic and functional purpose rather than being a standard aquarium filter or heater.

How it Works

The silver cylinder contains a small ceramic disk that vibrates at an incredibly high frequency (ultrasonic). When submerged in a shallow layer of water, these vibrations tear the water molecules apart, creating a cool, thick fog without using heat.

Common Uses

  • Terrariums & Aquariums: It's used to create a "swampy" or tropical look by letting fog roll across the surface of the water. It also helps maintain high humidity for tropical plants or amphibians.
  • Tabletop Fountains: Often used in decorative indoor water features for a "mystical" effect.
  • Hydroponics: Sometimes used in "aeroponic" systems to deliver moisture and nutrients directly to plant roots in mist form.

A Few Quick Tips

  • Water Level is Key: That black "stub" sticking out next to the silver ring is a water level sensor. If the water isn't deep enough to cover that sensor, the device won't turn on to prevent the ceramic disk from burning out.
  • Splash Guard: These tend to spit small droplets of water upward while misting, so they are usually used with a splash guard or placed in a deep enough container to keep the surrounding area dry.
  • Cleaning: Over time, mineral buildup from tap water can crust over the white disk. If it stops misting, a gentle soak in vinegar or a light wipe with a Q-tip usually fixes it.
